cases.sentence: ___ причиненном мужу, возбуждало в ней чувство, похожее на отвращение.
cases.translation: The memory of the wrong done to her husband aroused in her a feeling like disgust.
cases.explain: Воспоминание is the grammatical subject of возбуждало (aroused), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Она любила его за его самого и за его любовь к ___.
cases.translation: She loved him for himself and for his love for her.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving ней after a preposition.

cases.sentence: Чем больше она узнавала ___, тем больше она любила его.
cases.translation: The more she got to know Vronsky, the more she loved him.
cases.explain: Вронского is the direct object of узнавала (was learning about); animate masculine nouns take a genitive-form accusative.

cases.sentence: Наружность его, изменившаяся в ___ платье, была для нее привлекательна.
cases.translation: His appearance, changed by civilian dress, was attractive to her.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governing location/state takes the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Он скоро почувствовал, что осуществление его желания доставило ему только песчинку из той ___ счастья, которой он ожидал.
cases.translation: He soon felt that the realization of his desire had given him only a grain of sand from that mountain of happiness which he had expected.
cases.explain: The preposition из (out of) always governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Он остановился на живописи, стал заниматься ___, и в нее положил тот незанятый запас желаний.
cases.translation: He settled on painting, took up painting, and put into it that unoccupied store of desires.
cases.explain: The verb заниматься (to occupy oneself with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: И в таком роде он начал писать ___ Анны в итальянском костюме.
cases.translation: And in that style he began to paint a portrait of Anna in Italian costume.
cases.explain: Портрет is the direct object of the transitive verb писать (to paint), so it takes the accusative case.

reading.ru: Анна в этот первый период своего освобождения и быстрого выздоровления чувствовала себя непростительно счастливую и полную радости жизни.
reading.question: How did Anna feel during this first period after her recovery?
options: Inexcusably happy and full of joy of life
reading.correct: Inexcusably happy and full of joy of life
reading.explain: The text says Anna felt inexcusably happy and full of the joy of life.

reading.ru: Воспоминание несчастья мужа не отравляло ее счастье.
reading.question: Did the memory of her husband's misfortune poison Anna's happiness?
options: Yes, it constantly poisoned her happiness
No, it did not poison her happiness
It caused her to return to him
reading.correct: No, it did not poison her happiness
reading.explain: The text states the memory of her husband's misfortune did not poison her happiness.

reading.question: What metaphor does Anna use for her husband in relation to her own escape?
options: A drowning man who pulled someone down with him and drowned
A ship that sank in a storm
reading.correct: A drowning man who pulled someone down with him and drowned
reading.explain: Anna compares herself to a drowning person who tore away someone clinging to her, and that person (her husband) drowned.

reading.ru: Я лишаюсь честного имени и сына.
reading.question: What did Anna tell herself she was losing because of her actions?
options: Her honest name and her son
reading.correct: Her honest name and her son
reading.explain: Anna reflects that she is losing her honest name and her son.

reading.ru: Но как неискренно хотела Анна страдать, она не страдала.
reading.question: Despite wanting to suffer, did Anna actually suffer?
options: Yes, she suffered greatly every day
No, however insincerely she wished to suffer, she did not suffer
She suffered only when she saw her son
reading.correct: No, however insincerely she wished to suffer, she did not suffer
reading.explain: The text says that however insincerely Anna wanted to suffer, she did not suffer.

reading.ru: Разлука с сыном, которого она любила, и та не мучила ее первое время.
reading.question: Did the separation from her son torment Anna at first?
options: No, even that did not torment her at first
It tormented her only in dreams
It tormented Vronsky more than her
reading.correct: No, even that did not torment her at first
reading.explain: The text states that even the separation from her beloved son did not torment her during this early time.

reading.ru: Девочка, его ребенок, была так мила и так привязала к себе Анну с тех пор, как у ней осталась одна эта девочка, что Анна редко вспоминала о сыне.
reading.question: Why did Anna rarely think of her son during this time?
options: Because the baby girl, his child, so attached Anna to herself
Because she had forgotten she had a son
Because her son had written that he hated her
reading.correct: Because the baby girl, his child, so attached Anna to herself
reading.explain: The text explains that the little girl was so dear and attached Anna to herself that Anna rarely remembered her son.

reading.ru: Чем больше она узнавала Воронского, тем больше она любила его.
reading.question: What happened to Anna's love for Vronsky as she got to know him better?
options: It grew stronger the more she knew him
reading.correct: It grew stronger the more she knew him
reading.explain: The text says the more she learned about Vronsky, the more she loved him.

reading.ru: Ее восхищение пред ним часто пугало ее самое.
reading.question: How did Anna feel about her own admiration for Vronsky?
reading.explain: The text says her admiration for him often frightened her.

reading.ru: Он, по ее мнению, имевший такое определенное призвание к государственной деятельности, в которой должен был играть видную роль, он пожертвовал честолюбием для нее, никогда не показывая ни малейшего сожаления.
reading.question: What did Anna believe Vronsky had sacrificed for her?
options: His ambition for a prominent role in government service
reading.correct: His ambition for a prominent role in government service
reading.explain: The text says Vronsky, who had a clear calling for state service, sacrificed his ambition for her without showing regret.

reading.ru: Вронский, между тем, несмотря на полное осуществление того, что он желал так долго, не был вполне счастлив.
reading.question: Was Vronsky fully happy after achieving what he had long desired?
options: No, he was not fully happy despite achieving his desire
He was happy only when painting
He became happy only after leaving Anna
reading.correct: No, he was not fully happy despite achieving his desire
reading.explain: The text states that despite the full realization of what he had long wanted, Vronsky was not entirely happy.

reading.ru: 16 часов дня надо было занять чем-нибудь, так как они жили за границей на совершенной свободе, вне того круга условий общественной жизни, который занимал время в Петербурге.
reading.question: Why did Vronsky need to fill his time with activities abroad?
options: He lived in complete freedom abroad, without the social obligations that filled his time in Petersburg
He was training for a duel
reading.correct: He lived in complete freedom abroad, without the social obligations that filled his time in Petersburg
reading.explain: The text explains he had many hours to fill because he was free from the social circle that occupied his time in Petersburg.

reading.ru: И как голодное животное хватает всякий попадающийся предмет, надеясь найти в нем пищу, так и Вронский совершенно бессознательно хватался то за политику, то за новые книги, то за картины.
reading.question: What comparison is used to describe how Vronsky grasped at various pursuits?
options: A hungry animal grabbing at anything hoping to find food
reading.correct: A hungry animal grabbing at anything hoping to find food
reading.explain: The text compares Vronsky to a hungry animal grasping at whatever object it finds, hoping to find food in it.

reading.ru: Так как с молоду у него была способность к живописи, и так как он, не зная, куда тратить свои деньги, начал собирать гравюры, он остановился на живописи, стал заниматься ею, и в нее положил тот незанятый запас желаний, который требовал удовлетворения.
reading.question: Why did Vronsky settle on painting as his pursuit?
options: Because Anna insisted he take up a hobby
Because he had a talent for painting since youth and had begun collecting engravings
Because he wanted to sell paintings for money
reading.correct: Because he had a talent for painting since youth and had begun collecting engravings
reading.explain: The text says he had a youthful aptitude for painting and had started collecting engravings, so he settled on painting.

reading.ru: И в таком роде он начал писать портрет Анны в итальянском костюме, и портрет этот казался ему и всем, кто его видел, очень удачным.
reading.question: What did Vronsky paint, and how was it received?
options: A landscape that everyone found mediocre
A portrait of Anna in Italian costume that seemed very successful to him and everyone who saw it
A religious scene that was criticized
A portrait of Golenishchev that was never finished
reading.correct: A portrait of Anna in Italian costume that seemed very successful to him and everyone who saw it
reading.explain: The text says he began painting a portrait of Anna in Italian costume, which seemed very successful to him and all who saw it.
